clue.text: Lots of nameless numpties

indicators.note: nameless says the abbreviation for name, N, is dropped from the word

parts.note: numpties and noodles are both slang for fools

explanation.surface: Complaining that there are far too many idiots about.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the standard abbreviation for name; 'numpty' is Scottish slang for a fool, as is 'noodle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for a large quantity or great number of something.

clue.text: Flyer operating flaps

indicators.note: flaps means is in a flap, agitated, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pilot working the wing flaps of an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' and 'flaps' suggest aviation, but the flyer is a butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: A European butterfly whose males have bright coloured wing tips, so it flies.

clue.text: Stray cat heading off after daughter

indicators.note: after places the shortened cat following the daughter
heading off removes the first letter of the big cat

parts.note: a tigress is a female big cat

explanation.surface: A wandering cat setting off after a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to wander off the subject when speaking or writing.

clue.text: Unruly and merry, wants to shed clothing

indicators.note: shed clothing strips the outer letters from each word, leaving their insides

explanation.surface: A tipsy, rowdy person keen to strip off.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the sense of wayward or misbehaving, straying from proper conduct.

clue.text: Very strong wine imported by African country

indicators.note: imported by says the wine is brought inside the country's letters

parts.note: DRC is the Democratic Republic of the Congo
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A potent wine shipped into an African nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: drastic measures are extreme, severe or forceful in effect.

clue.text: Took out old hat

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: having courted someone, and being out of date.

clue.text: Pirates punished with variable harshness

indicators.note: punished means knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Y is a variable in algebra

explanation.surface: Buccaneers chastised with fluctuating severity.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: roughness or sharpness of manner or tone.

clue.text: Pilot put away food with a will

parts.note: a pilot study is a test or trial
to put away food is to eat it, past tense ate

explanation.surface: An aviator who eats with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With a will' suggests enthusiasm, but it means having made a legal will.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal term for someone who dies having left a valid will.

clue.text: Ally of NATO for example ignoring borders

indicators.note: ignoring borders drops the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: NATO is an acronym, a word formed from initial letters

explanation.surface: A NATO partner country that disregards frontiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a close friend or companion, often a political associate.

clue.text: Dance hall losing money twice over Prohibition period

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the shortened hall above the rest
L stands for pounds, money, and losing it twice removes two such letters

parts.note: the word hall is used as it stands
a ban is a prohibition
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A dance venue going broke during the Prohibition years.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow Cuban dance in duple time, famous from Bizet's Carmen.

clue.text: Infuriate supporter, changing sides

indicators.note: changing sides swaps the left-hand letter for the right-hand one, L becoming R

parts.note: an angel is a financial backer, especially of a theatre show

explanation.surface: Annoying a fan by defecting to the other team.
explanation.walkthrough: L and R are the abbreviations for left and right, the two sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to enrage or make someone furious.

clue.text: Article with hint concerning hors d'oeuvre

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a tip is a hint or piece of advice
'as to' means concerning or regarding

explanation.surface: A piece of writing offering advice about starters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian name for the starter course of cold meats, olives and vegetables before a meal.

clue.text: Inexperienced boy going round North Island

parts.note: green means naive or new to something

indicators.note: going round says the boy's letters enclose the abbreviation for North

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A naive lad touring a northern island.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the world's largest island, in the Arctic, a territory of Denmark.

clue.text: Eager, articulate commie chap shunned by many

indicators.note: articulate means spoken out loud, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: a 'reddy' is a red, a communist, someone many people would cold-shoulder

explanation.surface: A keen, well-spoken communist ostracised by most people.
explanation.walkthrough: Commie and red are both slang for a communist; the answer is pronounced exactly like 'reddy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being keen and willing to do something, as in 'ready to help'.

clue.text: Hard drinker knocked back moonshine

indicators.note: knocked back says the combined letters are turned around

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
a sot is a habitual drunkard

explanation.surface: A tough boozer downing illicit liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moonshine' looks like illegal spirits next to 'drinker' and 'knocked back', but it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine in its figurative sense is foolish talk or rubbish, a synonym of this slang word.

clue.text: Verses stir volatile attendant

indicators.note: volatile means unstable and changeable, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Poetry provokes an excitable waiting-staff member.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a female servant or waitress who attends on others.

clue.text: Cleaning car, see beer can on top of gearbox

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the can above the next letter

parts.note: V stands for vide, Latin for see
ale is a type of beer
a tin is a can

indicators.note: top of takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Car maintenance involving a beer can resting on the gearbox.
explanation.definitionFit: Valeting is the thorough cleaning of a vehicle's interior and exterior, as a service.

clue.text: Meaning of extremely strange male capers

indicators.note: extremely takes the outermost letters of the word

parts.note: antics are capers or pranks

explanation.surface: The significance of a man's bizarre pranks.
explanation.definitionFit: The branch of linguistics concerned with significance, and loosely the sense of words.

clue.text: The learned elite rationalise to an extent

indicators.note: to an extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The intellectual upper class partly justify themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective noun for educated, scholarly or literary people.

clue.text: Paying one to follow academic panel

indicators.note: to follow places the numeral after the academic

parts.note: prof is short for professor, an academic
I is the Roman numeral one
a table is a flat slab or panel

explanation.surface: A paid position on a university committee.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective synonym: a paying venture makes money, yielding a return.

clue.text: Tired old couple filling vase

indicators.note: filling says the pair goes inside the vase

parts.note: an urn is a vase
a couple is two

explanation.surface: An exhausted elderly pair stuffed into an urn.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: hackneyed, stale or worn out through overuse.

clue.text: Half-cut scally initially makes racket

indicators.note: half-cut says the word is cut in two and only its first half kept
initially says only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: a scally is Merseyside slang for a young rogue; the word is used as it stands

explanation.surface: A tipsy Liverpudlian rogue starting a din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' (drunk) and 'racket' (noise) suggest a rowdy scene; a scally is a Merseyside slang term for a roguish young man.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a fraudulent scheme or swindle, a synonym for a con.

clue.text: Reflective stud as yet uneasy in church

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: uneasy means unsettled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chunky earring worn uncomfortably in church.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflector set into the road to mark lanes at night, invented in Britain by Percy Shaw.

clue.text: Jellyfish in sea north of America

indicators.note: north of in a down clue places the sea above America

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
USA is the United States of America

explanation.surface: Jellyfish swimming in the ocean off North America.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoological term for the free-swimming bell-shaped form of a jellyfish.

clue.text: Article on father and pioneer of French film

indicators.note: on in an across clue places the article after the father

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about Dad and an early French filmmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Pathé founded a pioneering French film company famous for newsreels.

clue.text: Tartan pants left aesthete in distress at first

indicators.note: at first takes the first letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Checked trousers that left a fashionable dandy upset.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaid is a chequered tartan cloth, the shawl worn in Scottish Highland dress.

clue.text: Mate on the ground, the worse for wear

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A friend lying on the floor, rather battered.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally damaged by moths, figuratively shabby and worn out.

clue.text: Man turning up teaching bible material

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue reads the letters upwards, backwards

parts.note: IOM is the Isle of Man
RE is religious education, school teaching about scripture

explanation.surface: A man arriving to teach scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is religious education, a school subject in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A watered silk fabric with a rippling sheen, a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Vacuous Alfred and Oscar share deep love

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so only the outer letters of the name remain

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a ration is a fixed share or allowance

explanation.surface: Two men, one dim, sharing a passionate affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: worship or intense devoted affection for someone.

clue.text: Short-stay children's homes must recruit regularly

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Temporary care homes needing to hire staff on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to care homes; the definition is a playful description of wombs, where unborn children stay nine months.
explanation.definitionFit: Wombs house babies only briefly before birth, a witty periphrasis for the plural of uterus.

clue.text: Study point and bulk of tooth

parts.note: a den is a private study room
a tine is a prong or point, as of a fork

explanation.surface: Studying dentistry: a sharp end and most of a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard calcareous tissue forming most of a tooth beneath the enamel.

clue.text: Having tail extended worries pet

parts.note: cares are worries or anxieties
the tail, last letter, of the worries is extended by repeating it once more

explanation.surface: A pet animal anxious about its tail growing longer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having tail extended' doubles the final S of CARES; 'pet' looks like an animal but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to stroke or fondle affectionately.
